deep_dive.title: Efficient Provably Private Classification with a Tabular Foundation Model
deep_dive.abstract: Tabular data underpin prediction and decision-making in medicine, finance, government and science, but often contain sensitive individual-level information, creating a need for accurate prediction while preserving privacy. Traditional private learning provides formal privacy guarantees, but requires slow dataset-specific optimisation, suffers substantial utility loss under strong privacy, and is often difficult to apply correctly. Tabular foundation models adapt rapidly to new datasets, but existing models lack formal privacy guarantees, and are highly vulnerable to membership-inference attacks, limiting their use on sensitive data. Here we introduce PrivTab, an easy to use tabular foundation model for differentially private classification that embeds a privacy mechanism within its architecture. Pretrained on simulated datasets, PrivTab uses in-context learning to transform sensitive rows into compact, provably private summaries---effectively learning how to learn under privacy. PrivTab outperforms private linear and neural-network baselines under moderate-to-strong privacy, shows negligible membership leakage, maintains well-calibrated predictions under strong privacy, and reduces dataset fitting time by 10,000 times, requiring only a single forward pass. By combining formal privacy, speed, and easy of use, PrivTab brings recent advances in AI to applications where sensitive individual-level data have limited their adoption.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Tabular data often holds sensitive information, but traditional private learning is slow and loses utility while tabular foundation models lack privacy guarantees. PrivTab is an easy-to-use tabular foundation model for differentially private classification that adapts fast while providing formal privacy and resisting membership inference.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 表格数据广泛用于医疗、金融等敏感场景，但传统隐私学习需逐数据集优化、效用损失大，而现有表格基础模型缺乏隐私保证且易受成员推断攻击。本文提出PrivTab，一个易用的表格基础模型，用于差分隐私分类，兼顾快速适配与形式化隐私。实验表明其在强隐私约束下仍能保持较高分类精度。该工作拓展了表格基础模型在敏感数据上的可用性。

deep_dive.title: Thinking in Depth: Retrospective Inference for Tabular Foundation Models
deep_dive.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are pretrained across diverse tabular tasks and make predictions on a new table at inference time using its labeled examples as context. Most recent TFMs perform such in-context prediction with stacked Transformer layers, repeatedly transforming how examples are represented and compared. By tracing individual queries through several strong TFMs, we find that predictive refinement is highly uneven across depth and is often concentrated in later layers. This uneven refinement motivates us to reconsider how intermediate representations are constructed and reused throughout the network. We introduce Retro, a tabular foundation model based on retrospective inference, where later stages can explicitly revisit and recombine intermediate information produced earlier in the network. Retro organizes this process around two complementary operations: which intermediate information to revisit, and how the resulting contextual update should be shaped for each query. Attention Residuals address the former by adaptively reweighting contributions from different depths, while query-conditioned Gated Attention addresses the latter by modulating the attention output element-wise across representation dimensions. Our analysis shows that Retro shifts predictive refinement earlier and more broadly across depth, with different stages revising different subsets of queries in a pattern suggestive of multi-view refinement. Across TabArena, TALENT, and RelArena, Retro ranks among the top three and lies on the Pareto frontier. These results indicate that directly reusing intermediate representations provides a practical way to better exploit depth in TFMs.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对表格基础模型逐层预测细化在深度上高度不均、往往集中于靠后层而中间表示利用不足的问题，作者提出基于回溯推理的Retro模型。它让后续阶段显式重访并重组中间表示，改变逐层变换的方式。追踪多个强TFM的查询路径验证了细化不均现象，实验显示该设计改进了表示构建与复用，为表格基础模型的深度架构提供新思路。
